'''Emily Elspeth Witt''' is an American mathematician, an associate professor and Keeler Intra-University Professor of mathematics at the [[University of Kansas]]. Her research involves [[commutative algebra]], [[representation theory]], and [[singularity theory]].

==Education and career==
Witt is a 2005 graduate of the [[University of Chicago]], where she majored in mathematics with a specialization in computer science.{{r|cv}} She completed her Ph.D. in 2011 at the [[University of Michigan]]. Her dissertation, ''Local cohomology and group actions'', was supervised by [[Melvin Hochster]].{{r|mg}}

Witt worked as a Dunham Jackson Assistant Professor at the [[University of Minnesota]] from 2011 to 2014, and as a research assistant professor at the [[University of Utah]] from 2014 to 2015. In 20155, she obtained a tenure-track assistant professorship at the University of Kansas. She was promoted to associate professor in 2020,{{r|cv}} and named Keeler Intra-University Professor for 2021–2022.{{r|cv|keeler}}

==Recognition==
Witt is the 2022–2023 winner of the [[Ruth I. Michler Memorial Prize]] of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]].{{r|michler}}
